RGB.rescale <- function(mosaic, num.band) {

return(mosaic)}

Filipe

A função fornece a posição X e Y de cada objeto. Uma solução seria utilizar essa informação para criar um critério e ordenar a posição dos polígonos no R. #######################################

min.x<-do.call(c,lapply(EX.Obj.D$x.position,function(x){

  c(min(x[,1]))

  }))

for(i in 1:length(pos.min.x)){

}

messages.body_plain:
Hi Tony,

To evaluate plant height on small plots it is very important
to have a more precise GIS correction or geometric calibration to avoid weird
results. For example, using GCPs or having RTK-GPS on the drone. Please, take
the time to look at this example: https://filipematias23.github.io/FIELDimageR-Workshop-10/#example-02

In this example, I was working with an orthomosaic with no
geometric calibration. My intention was to evaluate plat height for different populations
of potatoes (from left to right are T1, T2, T3, and T4). In the image below, I
plotted the value extracted per plot for all trials. Apparently, seems that T1 (bluer)
is at least 1 meter taller than T4 (redder), but that is not true. It happens
because I extracted the data without removing the soil base. What we are seeing
is the effect of slope in the terrain.

Trying to adapt to your case, maybe because you didn’t correct
the geographic position between your soil base and the orthomosaic with plants,
the alignment of plots is not good generating a bad calculation of the canopy
height model (CHM). One possible solution is using instead the DEM from soil
base flight will be to use the Digital Terrain Model (DTM) from the same
orthomosaic with plants. In other words, the idea is to use the CHM=DEM-DTM
from the same flight. Is that make sense? For future evaluations of plant
height think about using GCPs… ok

Hope that helps…!!!

All the best,

Filipe

Olá de novo e já me perdoem por incomodá-los.

Estou tentando fazer esse código funcionar, mas quando defino a lista de imagens sendo pics, ocorre um erro por não reconhecer o objeto (pics), a partir daí começam a correr outros erros.
Se alguém puder me ajudar, segue o script
Preciso da contagem de plantas e porcentagem de área coberta.

### START ###
####################################################################################
# clean data :
####################################################################################
remove (list=ls())

# Required packages

library(parallel)

library(foreach)

library(doParallel)

library(FIELDimageR)

library(raster)

# Images names (folder directory: "./images/")

pics<-list.files("C:/Users/gujac/Documentos/FIELDimageR/images/")

# Vegetation indices

index<- c("BGI")

################

### Parallel ###

################

# Number of cores

n.core<-detectCores()-1

# Starting parallel

cl <- makeCluster(n.core, output = "")

registerDoParallel(cl)

system.time({

               EX.Table.Parallel<- foreach(i = 1:length(pics), .packages = c("raster","FIELDimageR"),

                               .combine = rbind) %dopar% {

                                 EX.L1<-stack(paste("./images/",pics[i],sep = ""))

                                 EX.L1<-aggregate(EX.L1,fact=4) #Reducing image resolution (fast analysis)

                                 EX.L.Shape<-fieldPolygon(mosaic=EX.L1, extent=T, plot=F) # extent=T (The whole image area will be the shapefile)

                                 EX.L2<-fieldMask(mosaic=EX.L1, index="BGI", cropValue=0.8, cropAbove=T, plot=F) # Select one index to identify leaves and remove the background

                                 EX.L4<-fieldIndex(mosaic=EX.L2$newMosaic, index=index, plot=F) # Indices

                                 EX.L.Info <http://EX.L.Info><- fieldInfo(mosaic=EX.L4[[index]], fieldShape=EX.L.Shape$fieldShape, projection=F) # projection=F (Ignore projection. Normally used only with remote sensing images)

                                 EX.L.Info <http://EX.L.Info>$plotValue # Combine information from all images in one table

                              }})

rownames(EX.Table.Parallel)<-pics

EX.Table.Parallel

### END ###
